result.summary: This PR adds a new microbenchmark, WalletBalanceManySpent, that builds a wallet with ~50,000 historical TXOs where nearly all are spent and only ~50 remain unspent, then measures GetBalance() performance. It was written specifically to validate the performance claims of PR #27865, which separates spent from spendable TXOs. The PR also refactors shared fake-block-generation helper code out of wallet_create_tx.cpp into wallet_bench_util.h so both benchmarks can reuse it.
result.problem: Wallets with heavy transaction history (Lightning nodes, exchanges, payment processors) can accumulate large numbers of spent TXOs, and there is currently no benchmark demonstrating how GetBalance() scales with that history, making it hard to quantify proposed optimizations like #27865.

l0rinc asked for a comment explaining forward-compatible dead code for #27865, author has not replied to this specific point yet.

result.card: This PR adds a WalletBalanceManySpent benchmark simulating a wallet with ~50,000 historical TXOs, nearly all spent, to measure GetBalance() performance, and refactors shared fake-block-generation helpers for benchmarks. It exists specifically to validate PR #27865's claimed optimization, and the author reports a ~2,981x speedup with that PR applied versus master. Review has been thorough: l0rinc left many detailed inline suggestions, the author implemented nearly all of them across two commits and credited l0rinc as co-author, and l0rinc gave an ACK on a specific commit. The PR currently shows 'Needs rebase' and 'CI failed' labels despite a force-push on 2026-08-18, so its exact current reviewable state is uncertain. As pure test infrastructure with no direct user impact, its priority rests on the leverage it provides toward reviewing and merging #27865.
